findings.where: First screen, the row of five outlined pills under the lead paragraph (PPP Law, Infrastructure, Development banks, Governments, Risk allocation), at both widths
findings.fault: The five topics look like filter chips or topic links. Each is a separate rounded box with a white outline and semibold sans label, sitting just above the one action. None of them can be clicked (parts p10–p14 are static). A visitor who taps 'PPP Law' expecting his PPP work or articles gets nothing. The chip shape belongs to selectable or linked parts, and here it is used for plain facts.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer scanning for Mark's PPP law experience, who taps the pill they care about and finds it dead. Each pill is a false affordance one row above the real action, so it also weakens how clearly the email button reads as the only thing to press.

findings.where: First screen, the primary action 'Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com →' (white button beside 'Write to me at'), at both widths
findings.fault: The page's one action points to '#' (part p16), not to a mailto: for the address it shows. Clicking or tapping it opens no mail and goes nowhere. The arrow also suggests it leads to another page rather than opening an email.
findings.who_objects: Any visitor who decides to contact Mark, which is the brand sheet's one action. They press the most prominent control on the page and nothing happens, so they have to copy the address by hand.

findings.where: Article specimen: the lecture link 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the 'Abundance' Challenge' and the list bullets above it, against 'Play again' in the motion sketch
findings.fault: The page uses two link colours. The lecture link is underlined orange-red, while 'Play again' and the palette's stated link colour are house blue. The same orange-red also marks the static list bullets, so a static part takes the link colour. A reader can't learn one look for 'this goes somewhere'.
findings.who_objects: Angélique and later readers of article pages, where links in prose matter most. A link colour that changes between parts, and also appears on static bullets, makes them unsure which coloured text they can follow.
